arena.name: retrieval-arena
arena.title: Retrieval Arena
arena.question: Which retrieval setup finds the existing story a new item belongs to, so enable-ai's feed doesn't show the same news twice?

headline: Use **hybrid-voyage** (recall@5 96%, right story first 82%, 245ms median, $0.0118 per 1k). Production today (its logged decisions): 90.9% correct end to end; 31% of items that belong to an existing story became a duplicate story, and 2% of all items were merged into the wrong story. Production's logged candidates contained the right story for 84.5% of matching items, so 15% never reached the judge. openai-3-large reaches 97.3% (paired McNemar p=0.0005).

pick.name: hybrid-voyage
pick.reason: recall@5 96.4%, right story first 82% of the time (MRR 0.89), 245ms median, $0.012 per 1k items.

labels.note: Model labels, cross-checked, with disputes reviewed. Where labeler and production made the same mistake the label is wrong too, which favors production.

data.description: 470 real items and 491 stories exported read-only from enable-ai production; scored on items that belong to an existing story.

method.rules: Tied = within 2% of the best score and not significantly worse (exact McNemar, p < 0.05); pick = best combined cost and latency rank among tied. Score is end-to-end accuracy when the run has it, else recall@5.

outcome.note: Finding - production's 0.10 cosine cutoff dropped the right story for 15% of matching items; 0.20 recovers most. Link the enable-ai change here once it ships.

caveats: Labels come from models, not humans.
A correct story that none of the pooled retrievers found was never labeled.
One workload; with ~110 matching items, treat gaps of a couple of points as noise.
Latency is one laptop through OpenRouter, network included.
